Who I Am
A Tax & Accounting Professional
with Purpose

I am Md. Saiful Islam, currently working as Assistant Manager — Accounts & Tax at Quazi Enterprises Ltd., Dhaka. I bring 10+ years of hands-on experience in accounts, finance, VAT, tax compliance, withholding tax, annual return support, ERP-based reporting, and regulatory communication.

My core strengths include financial statements, monthly MIS, bank reconciliation, supplier bill verification, loan reconciliation, TDS/VDS/withholding records, annual return documentation, NBR hearing support, and accounting controls.

I hold First Class MBS and BBS degrees in Accounting from National University, am an NBR Authorised Income Tax Practitioner (ITP), and am a CMA Intermediate Candidate at ICMAB with 1 paper pending.

Research & Publications
Research & Publications

A research-focused profile designed for Finance Leadership & HR review, demonstrating practical exposure to digital tax administration, corporate tax compliance risk, IFRS-based reporting, and Bangladesh-focused regulatory practice.

Working Paper Abstract ID: 6894598 WPS Date: 07.06.2026

E-VAT Adoption and VAT Revenue Performance in South Asia: Evidence from Bangladesh

Md. Saiful Islam
Senior Executive, Tax & VAT Department, Quazi Enterprises Ltd., Dhaka, Bangladesh

Abstract

Electronic Value Added Tax (E-VAT) schemes play an important role in modernizing tax administration in South Asia, but revenue effects vary widely across countries with similar policy goals. The study examines E-VAT maturity, VAT/GST revenue performance, taxpayer behaviour, and implementation challenges in selected South Asian economies, with specific reference to Bangladesh.

View full abstract
This study follows a sequential explanatory mixed methods design, using secondary country-year data for fiscal years 2019-2024 and 25 semi-structured interviews with 5 NBR officials, 10 VAT consultants and 10 VAT-registered SME taxpayers. Due to the small panel sample (n = 25), the exploratory OLS regression analysis is not intended to establish exact causal relationships. Although Bangladesh has a 15% standard VAT rate and an operational E-VAT platform since 2019, Bangladesh records a low VAT-to-GDP ratio of about 3.6%, compared with Nepal (5.3%), India (6-7%) and the Maldives (approximately 12%). Interview evidence highlights institutional and operational barriers, including segregated revenue databases, portal unreliability during peak e-invoice filing, low taxpayer training, weak grievance mechanisms, and the absence of mandatory e-invoicing. The study suggests the Bangladesh E-VAT Adoption Framework (BEVAF), linking institutional enablers, technology platform maturity, and behavioural compliance outcomes. The findings support a staged reform program focused on e-invoicing, database integration, taxpayer assistance, audit risk scoring, mobile invoice access, and penalty procedure reform.
Keywords: E-VAT; Digital Tax Administration; VAT Compliance; Bangladesh; South Asia; TAM; E-Governance; Revenue Mobilization; SME; BEVAF JEL: H25, H26, H83, O38, O53
Empirical Accounting & Taxation Research 2nd Paper

Corporate Tax Compliance Risk under IFRS-Based Financial Reporting: Multi-Case Evidence from Emerging Market Companies

Md. Saiful Islam
Senior Executive, Tax & VAT Department, Quazi Enterprises Ltd., Dhaka, Bangladesh
Manuscript type: Empirical accounting and taxation research paper

Abstract

This study explores corporate tax compliance risk under IFRS-based financial reporting in an emerging market context through multi-case evidence from Bangladesh, combining country-level enterprise survey evidence, listed-company annual report data, and anonymized private-firm audit-work paper evidence.

View full abstract
The paper uses country-level enterprise survey evidence, listed company annual report data from Square Pharmaceuticals PLC and Grameenphone Ltd, and public evidence from annual reports supplemented by anonymized audit-work paper evidence from two private companies. The evidence indicates that statutory tax rates alone do not determine corporate tax compliance risk. Risk is also influenced by regulatory time cost, interaction with tax officials, firm size, deferred tax effects, cash tax settlement, and estimated book-tax differences. The World Bank Enterprise Survey Bangladesh 2022 reports that 51.0% of firms were visited by or had to meet tax officials, with the highest interaction rate among large firms at 71.6%. Listed-company evidence shows variation in ETR, cash ETR, current tax expense, deferred tax income and estimated BTD by sector. The anonymized private-firm evidence adds practical depth by showing how audit-work paper tax numbers can help interpret tax risk in unlisted companies. The study contributes to accounting and taxation literature by connecting IFRS-based reporting, tax administration, and practitioner-level compliance risk in an emerging market setting.
Keywords: Corporate tax compliance; IFRS; effective tax rate; cash effective tax rate; book-tax differences; deferred tax; Bangladesh; emerging markets
